people.name: Plato
people.biography: A philosopher whose dialogues investigate justice, knowledge and the examined life. The dramatic Socrates in these works is not simply interchangeable with Plato.

people.name: Aristotle
people.biography: Breadth across disciplines supports leading historical consideration. Influence does not certify current scientific correctness.

people.name: Immanuel Kant
people.biography: Several reception routes support a leading position. Exact position against non-European traditions is unresolved.

people.name: Confucius
people.biography: Long reception supports a high historical case. Received text and historical person need separation.

people.name: David Hume
people.biography: Scholarly and comparative selections support high standing. Contemporary historical fame differs from later philosophical fame.

people.name: Avicenna / Ibn Sīnā
people.biography: Cross-disciplinary and interreligious reception supports a high place. Medicine and philosophy contribute different kinds of influence.

people.name: Nāgārjuna
people.biography: Buddhist reception across Asia supports high historical consideration. Work attributions are not uniformly secure.

people.name: Thomas Aquinas
people.biography: Scholastic reception supports upper-group consideration. A comparative worldwide rank needs more than reference coverage.

people.name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
people.biography: Language and method provide a strong historical case. Do not flatten contested phases into two simple doctrines.

people.name: Śaṅkara
people.biography: Vedānta reception supports an upper historical group. Religious authority and philosophical argument need separate evaluation.

people.name: Baruch Spinoza
people.biography: Critical, editorial and reader evidence support inclusion. Reader enthusiasm is self-selected.

people.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
people.biography: Psychological and value critique supports high standing. Authored works must be separated from notebook compilations.

people.name: Simone de Beauvoir
people.biography: Independent contribution merits more than derivative status. Do not reduce the corpus to one book.

people.name: al-Ghazālī
people.biography: Philosophical criticism and later reception support inclusion. Reject unsupported philosophy-decline shorthand.

people.name: Mencius
people.biography: Comparative ethics supports substantial historical consideration. Text compilation is distinct from personal authorship.

people.name: Hannah Arendt
people.biography: Public and scholarly reception supports inclusion. Different books and controversies require separate treatment.

people.name: John Rawls
people.biography: Institutional and international reception support inclusion. National reception produces conflicting political interpretations.

people.name: Frantz Fanon
people.biography: Africana and postcolonial reception sustain the historical case. Further independent debate over violence remains needed.

people.name: Mozi
people.biography: A thinker associated with the Mohist tradition. The received text also reflects later members of the school, so the collective corpus is not treated as single-person authorship.

people.name: John Stuart Mill
people.biography: Canonical argument supports historical inclusion. Colonial exclusions complicate a universalist reading.

people.name: B. R. Ambedkar
people.biography: Indian political reception supports a substantial case. A book-level comparison does not measure the whole philosopher.

people.name: Mary Wollstonecraft
people.biography: Feminist philosophical reception supports consideration. More work-specific and comparative evidence needed.

people.name: Mullā Ṣadrā
people.biography: Later Islamic philosophy challenges a truncated historical canon. English availability must be verified for a particular entry work.
